title: The network works, the public loses
chapter: The network works, the public loses
lines: The internet can work beautifully while the communities inside it lose the power to question its rules.
The Captured Internet argues that useful services became governing powers when communities could no longer challenge their rules.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Understand platform power through the governance problems that made its useful concentration possible.
emotionalPlan.visualActing: Show active human community and functioning connections together, avoiding a generic broken-internet image.
voiceDirections: Quiet concern; gently emphasize “question its rules”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “challenge their rules”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

sentenceIntentions.text: The internet can work beautifully while the communities inside it lose the power to question its rules.

title: A service becomes a government
lines: Its history begins with problems that simply connecting people did not solve.
Hosting, search, moderation, and security made shared services useful, then made them harder to leave.

title: Who decides what you see?
lines: The book follows how those services gained power over what people see and whom they trust.
What can a community control when its relationships and memories depend on someone else’s platform?

title: What would make departure possible?
lines: The inquiry takes both the work of keeping a service useful and the danger of concentrated power seriously.
Begin with a service you value, and ask when its convenience starts setting the rules.
